name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of all 23 tutorial steps (0-22) with per-step screenshots for visual regression testing. Exercises the tutorial overlay from start through congratulations, capturing each step's UI state, highlight targets, and progress indicator. Every player-facing step is a real click gated by the tutorial's own rail (issue #479/Finding #74 follow-up), including the box-cut and haul-debris stages the file originally skipped entirely.

steps.description: #553: confirming the grid now only ORDERS the 9 holes -- drill_hole became queued, vehicle-gated work, so they are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, and the tutorial does not advance to `charge` until they have landed. The wait is the step below; the mid-pattern screenshot above is the ghosts-and-real-holes picture #553 asks for. Start corrected from the file's original 15,15 to 20,20 (Finding #74/#75 follow-up): the tutorial's drill-plan stage gates its picker to REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts). #601-followup: REGION.drill is actually `{ x1: 20, z1: 20, x2: 26, z2: 26, exact: true }` -- the prior Finding #74/#75 note here claimed a larger grid and hole count than the tool actually produces, which was never real: a direct `drill_plan show` probe after the real drag+confirm read back spacing 3m but only a 3x3/9-hole grid landing at (20,20)-(26,26), matching REGION.drill's own real x2/z2 exactly, not the wider rectangle the note assumed. `dragTiles`'s x2/z2 corrected from 30,30 to 26,26 (the requested corners get clamped to `exact: true`'s own gate regardless, but the declared numbers should say what the gate actually allows, not a rectangle a real player's drag will never produce) and the command's rows/cols corrected from 4/4 back to 3/3, restoring this file's own original 9-hole declaration. spacing and depth both corrected from the file's original 5/8 to the grid tool's real defaults 3/6 (DEFAULT_SPACING_M/DEFAULT_DEPTH_M, Drill.ts), discovered live: neither stepper (#bs-param-strip [data-field="spacing"|"depth"]) is one of this stage's own targets (tutorialStages.ts's 'drill-plan' entry lists only the toolbar, grid-tool button, and picker canvas/confirm) -- the tutorial rail's own CSS lockout makes every other control pointer-events:none while a stage is active. CI cash mismatch fix: this command was also missing `diameter:`, the established diameter-omission bug (Finding #52 class) -- command mode defaults to 0.15 while the real Drill panel always sends DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), and computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole duration by diameter/0.15, so the omitted-diameter command mode this file's cash values were derived from kept the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) longer than a real click would. Added `diameter:0.089` to match the real click; every downstream checkpoint through the blast step was re-derived from command mode with the fix applied.

#553: the driller drives the rig to all 9 ordered holes and sinks them one at a time. A lone driller with no living quarters collapses from fatigue partway through and resumes, which is why the pad is this large -- sandbox-measured. #586 CI follow-up: this step used to be role:'player' driving `waitForTutorialStep(stepId:'charge')` to hold the real clock -- but the 'drill-plan' tutorial stage (tutorialSteps.ts/tutorialStepHelpers.ts's createComparisonStep) completes the instant `drillHoles.length` first exceeds its snapshot, i.e. after the FIRST of the 9 holes lands, not after all of them. waitForTutorialStep's own poll loop breaks the moment the rail reaches 'charge', which on a real CI run landed with only 1 of 9 holes drilled (orderedHoleCount dropped, not 0) -- a genuine early-exit in the rail's own gating, not pacing flakiness, so a longer timeout could never have fixed it (the loop does not wait out the timeout, it exits on the very next 200ms poll once the rail flips). Switched to the same hand-measured `tick N`, role:'setup' pattern `.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md` already documents for 'a wait for queued work to land' and that tutorial-playthrough.json/blast-basic.json already use for this identical post-drill_plan wait: the console `tick 400` command runs the full 400 ticks synchronously in one browser-JS turn, landing all 9 holes before the tutorial's own 250ms-interval poll (TutorialOverlay's tickGuide) ever gets a chance to observe the first one and flip the rail early. The `wait 500ms` after it just lets that poll catch up so `expect.tutorialStep` below reads the post-tick rail state rather than a stale pre-tick one. #616 (origin/main) confirmed the drill grid as 3x3/9-hole as part of its own tick-budget fix; #555 (this merge) layers the box-cut/rock-digger steps in front of it on the same real ticked clock, so `holeCount` here reads 9, matching the grid this file actually orders. #681 follow-up: this final chunk is 8/8 of the `tick 400` this step used to run as one unbroken block -- see 1/8 above for why it was split (revoltImmune removal, no intermediate checkpoint for the scheduler otherwise). Same total elapsed ticks (8*50=400), same final assertions below, unchanged.

expect.note: #555 regression guard: the box-cut+drill-plan stretch above is ~250+ ticks of two employees' continuous vehicle-gated work with no living_quarters anywhere in this file's own script -- exactly the pacing that drove wellBeing to a permanent 0 and a worker_revolt game-over here before this fix (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay had a dead zone at exactly 0: nothing but a strictly positive per-tick delta could ever move a score pinned at the clamped floor, and LevelDef.scoreDecayRate was declared per-level -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- but never actually reached updateScores, which always ran the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Asserting levelEndReason stays null right here, before charge/sequence/blast ever run, is what keeps a future pacing stretch from hiding a revolt behind this file's own closing `campaign complete` debug override again. #681 follow-up: `LevelDef.revoltImmune` (which used to make tutorial_pit immune to worker_revolt outright) is gone -- this block now has to survive the real rules, which is why it is split into eight `tick 50` steps instead of one `tick 400` (see 1/8 above).

#554-followup round 4 (issue #586 CI): rounds 1-3's fix (chunked tick-N/event-choose-0 rounds, 9x25 then consolidated to 3x100/3x75) still stalled intermittently in real interaction-mode CI -- root-caused via local reproduction to a genuine deadlock in the tutorial rail's own clock-hold logic (tutorialGuide.ts's decideClock/workSignature), not a tick-budget sizing problem. `createComparisonStep`'s isComplete (tutorialStepHelpers.ts) fires the instant its tracked count first ticks up past its snapshot, so the 'charge' tutorial stage (tutorialSteps.ts) advances to 'sequence' after the FIRST of 9 holes charges, not after all of them, since charging is real queued work post-#554 (was instant pre-#554) -- the same root cause already found and fixed for the 'drill-plan' stage's own tick-400 step above. Fixed at the source (tutorialSteps.ts): both 'charge' and 'sequence' steps now carry `waitsOnWork: true`, but that alone isn't sufficient -- TutorialOverlay's 250ms-interval tickGuide poll runs on a real setInterval, so ANY chunked-tick pattern that returns control to the JS event loop between ticks gives it a chance to fire mid-charge, and once it holds the clock (state.isPaused=true) the deadlock is permanent: every subsequent scenario `tick N` command is capped to exactly 1 real tick per call (events.ts's tickCommand loop checks `if (state.isPaused) break` at the END of each iteration), so real progress crawls far too slowly for the rail's own WORK_GRACE_TICKS(40)-tick recovery window to ever close before this file's own remaining tick budget runs out. Splitting the budget into fewer, bigger rounds (3x100, 3x75) only reduced the number of vulnerable gaps, it didn't close them -- reproduced the identical permanent stall at chargedCount=7 in two independent local runs regardless of chunk shape. Switched to the exact same single-giant-tick pattern the drill-plan step above already uses successfully: one synchronous `tick 225` call blocks the JS main thread for its entire duration, so the poll's setInterval callback cannot fire until it returns -- by which point all 9 holes are already charged and decideClock never gets a chance to observe a mid-charge gap at all. 225 ticks matches this session's earlier chunked-budget total (comfortable margin over the ~215 measured).

The real driver is #558's site growth alone: on the grown 48x48 site the spawn point resolves to (26, 24), which lands on the real 3x3/spacing-3 drill grid's own footprint (x:20-26, z:20-26) -- x=26 sits exactly on the grid's east edge, z=24 well inside it. (The prior write-up here cited a furthest-throw distance for a drill grid size that was never real -- see the drill_plan step's own #601-followup note -- so that figure is dropped rather than restated unverified for the real grid.) cash is unaffected either way (lawsuits/fines from a death do not deduct immediately). The #571 origin-offset regression itself is covered separately by the unit/integration tests added in 75a06cf, which force a negative origin (x:-4, z:-4). CI cash mismatch fix: cash corrected 70320 -> 70648 (+$328) now that the drill_plan step above carries `diameter:0.089` -- command mode's own drill_rig spent less time (and fuelCostPerTick) sinking all 9 holes once its duration matches what a real click always produced, so more cash survives to this checkpoint. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): that +$328 offset was correct relative to command mode, but the box-cut step several steps up this same file also turned out to carry a real-time-accrual error that compounds forward -- dropped the exact cash figure here too rather than chase a second moving target. Not replaced with `decreased`: as the note above already says, cash is unaffected by this step in either mode (command mode's own trace shows it completely unchanged), so there is no single mode-agnostic cash claim to make -- holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount/deathCount remain exact since they are not host-timing-sensitive. #555 tutorial worker-revolt fix (this PR): a real fix, not a route-around -- the preceding box-cut/drill-plan stretch used to crash wellBeing to a permanently-pinned 0 and flip `state.levelEndReason` to `worker_revolt` before this step ever ran (ScoreManager.ts's `applyDecay` had a dead zone at exactly 0, and `LevelDef.scoreDecayRate` -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- had never actually reached `updateScores`, which always used the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Both are fixed now: `state.levelEndReason` stays null through this step and for the rest of the run, `BlastReportModal` opens and renders normally post-blast (its `state.levelEndReason !== null` guard never trips), and this step is back to a real click sequence identical to tutorial-interactive.json's own proven blast step -- `report-close` is genuinely reachable again, not a permanent dead end.

#553: contract id renumbered 1 -> 23 for command mode (whose own, much shorter tick trajectory reaches this point with far fewer contract-pool refreshes behind it -- REFRESH_INTERVAL, Contract.ts -- so 23 is a valid, existing id there; verified live, command mode's own full run passes with it). Interaction mode's `interaction` array intentionally targets a *different* id, 24: same class of command/interaction divergence this file already documents repeatedly for cash (real per-click waiting racks up far more elapsed ticks than command mode's scripted count), extended here to which contract ids exist and what they demand. #586 CI follow-up, live-traced with a temporary `contract list` step inserted right above this one (removed again once diagnosed): at the tick interaction mode actually reaches this step, the pool held ids 22-29, and id 23 specifically was `Deliver blingite ore` -- a material this pit's own blast never produces (verified via `state full`: every one of its ~1900 fragments carries only `dirtite`/`rustite` in `oreDensities`, several with `{}` entirely; `blingite` appears nowhere). `ContractsPanel.makeActiveCard`'s Deliver button is `disabled` whenever `maxDeliverable <= 0` (`min(remainingKg, storedOf(materialId))` — `ContractsPanel.ts`), so accepting #23 there makes the delivery step below permanently unclickable by any real player, not just a scenario-authoring slip: a genuine contract/geology mismatch this specific run's luck-of-the-draw produced.
